opus-5.5* meaning_fix: I'm not convinced / it doesn't sit right with me / I don't buy it
opus-5.5* reasoning: Feminine participle faayte plus -li (it isn't going in for me). It expresses not being convinced more than not being able to cope.
gpt-6.1-sol* meaning_fix: It isn't sinking in / I can't get my head around it.
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: This is a feminine participle with the attached -li, figuratively describing an idea not getting through. It concerns comprehension or acceptance, not necessarily an inability to cope.
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: Idiomatic formula meaning it does not make sense to me / I cannot accept it; مش is mish.
opus-5 reasoning: mish negates the participle, as Palestinian requires. The feminine participle faayte plus the dative -li gives faaytitli; the exact vowel of that linking syllable varies between speakers.
opus-4.8 reasoning: mish + faytit 'entering' + -li; idiom 'it won't go into my head / I can't be bothered'.
sonnet-5.5 meaning_fix: it won't sink in / I can't get my head around it (said of a feminine thing)
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: faayit is Palestinian for 'entering' (from faat), here feminine faayt-at + li, 'it isn't getting into me'. It is about grasping or accepting something, not 'handling' it. A masculine subject would be mish faayitli.
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: Feminine participle agrees with an understood idea or matter and idiomatically means it will not sink in.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Idiomatic expression that something does not make sense to me or is beyond me.

meaning_fixes: and on the other hand

gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: A conversational transition meaning 'and on the other hand' or 'from another angle.' ثانية is pronounced taanye, with urban t rather than th.
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: Conjunctive phrase meaning from another perspective. Thaa in second is pronounced as taa in spoken Palestinian (taanye).
opus-5 meaning_fix: and on the other hand
opus-5 reasoning: ث in thaanye is pronounced t, so the Arabic is respelt تَانْيِة. The phrase introduces a contrast, so on the other hand is closer than from another perspective.
opus-4.8 reasoning: ث of ثانية becomes t: taanye. jihe side, lit. and from another side = on the other hand.
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: ثانية is taanye, with ث as t and taa marbuta as e. Taa marbuta after ه is also e. The phrase is a discourse connector meaning 'and on the other hand'.
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: This wording is formal. Conversation more naturally uses w min naa7ye taanye.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: From another perspective.

meaning_fixes: burst / popped / cracked; (slang) snapped, lost it / popped / cracked / banged; struck or made a quick trip in particular slang expressions
opus-5.5* meaning_fix: burst / popped / cracked; (slang) snapped, lost it
opus-5.5* reasoning: Ta'' is a crack or pop; slang Ta'' (or Ta''at ma3o) = he lost it or blew up. It doesn't mean went.
gpt-6.1-sol* meaning_fix: popped / cracked / banged; struck or made a quick trip in particular slang expressions
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: The basic sense involves a sudden pop, crack, or bang. 'Went' is construction-dependent, as in طقّ مشوار, rather than an unrestricted equivalent of 'went.'
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: Slang verb used in idioms like Ta'' mashwaar (went on an errand/trip). Taa is emphatic capital T and qaaf is glottalised to ''.
opus-5 meaning_fix: popped / burst / banged; in slang also took off, went
opus-5 reasoning: Geminate verb: ط is emphatic T and the shadda doubles the glottal ق. The basic sense is a pop or a knock, with the going-off sense an extension of it.

gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: This slang verb is highly context-dependent; went or hit alone is too vague. Final ق is glottalized and doubled.
gpt-5.6-terra meaning_fix: popped / struck; in slang, went suddenly
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Meaning is context-sensitive slang.

english: He's stingy (lit: his eye is narrow)
meaning_fixes: He's begrudging / envious, can't bear others having things (also stingy)
opus-5.5* meaning_fix: He's begrudging / envious, can't bear others having things (also stingy)
opus-5.5* reasoning: Dayy'a with emphatic D and glottal ق; ending a after ق. The idiom leans toward envy / begrudging others rather than plain stinginess, though both are heard.
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: A familiar idiom for someone stingy or begrudging. The adjective is contracted in conversational pronunciation, and ق is glottalized.
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: Everyday Palestinian idiom meaning stingy or envious. ض is emphatic D, ق is urban glottal stop ', and taa marbuta after ق is a.
opus-5 reasoning: 3een has ee plus the possessive -o. Dayy'a has emphatic ض as D, shadda on ي and ق as a glottal stop; taa marbuta after ق is a. Idiomatic for stingy or small-minded.
opus-4.8 reasoning: Idiom; Dayy'a has emphatic ض and glottal ق (kept as ق). 'His eye is narrow' = stingy.
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: ay becomes ee in urban speech (3eeno). ض is emphatic D, and ق is a glottal stop, so Dayyi'a. The idiom means stingy or tight-fisted, and is also heard as greedy.
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: Local idiom associating a narrow eye with stinginess.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: This idiom literally says that his eye is narrow and means that he is stingy. ض is emphatic.

opus-5.5* reasoning: khalaS 3alayy is commonly said to take something on (leave it to me). For I'm done for people more often say raa7at 3alayy or khilSat. Uncertain what the entry intends.
gpt-6.1-sol* meaning_fix: He/it finished me off / did me in
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: خلّص على means to finish someone off, with doubled ل. It can imply being done for, but راحت علي is a more direct expression for 'it's over for me.'
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: Everyday Palestinian expression meaning it is all over for me or I am finished, with emphatic S in khalaS.
opus-5 reasoning: ص is emphatic S. The past khiliS is the it-finished form, not the interjection khalaS; 3ala plus the first-person suffix doubles the y.
opus-4.8 reasoning: khalaS (emphatic S) it's finished + 3alayy on me (shadda on ي): I'm done for.
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: خلص is 'finished', with emphatic S. عليّ is 3alayy. Reads as 'it's over for me'. With a doubled l (khallaS 3alayy) it would mean 'he finished me off'.
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: As an idiomatic exclamation this means it is over for me; context distinguishes other readings.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: I am done for.

meaning_fixes: put himself on a par with him / took him on as an equal
opus-5.5* meaning_fix: put himself on a par with him / took him on as an equal
opus-5.5* reasoning: Literally put his head to his head. It suggests treating oneself as someone's equal or rival, often someone of higher standing, rather than just confronting him.
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: The idiom means taking someone on or confronting him, not literally placing two heads together. رأس is spoken raas, without its written hamza.
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: ح is 7, ط is doubled emphatic capital TT; 3ms suffix is -o (raaso). Standard idiom for confronting someone head-on.
opus-5 reasoning: Geminate 7aTT with emphatic T. راس, not رأس, is the Palestinian form, and the preposition bi- clitic gives braaso.
opus-4.8 reasoning: 7aTT (ط emphatic, shadda) 'put' + raaso b-raaso. Idiom for confronting head-on.
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: Idiom 'put his head against his head', meaning he faced him directly as an equal. The verb is 7aTT with emphatic doubled T, and the -o suffix means his.
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: Idiomatic phrase for setting oneself directly against someone.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Idiomatic expression for confronting someone head-on.

meaning_fixes: vouched for it absolutely (lit. put his hand in the fire); also took a big risk / put his hand in the fire; took a risk / vouched for someone
opus-5.5* meaning_fix: vouched for it absolutely (lit. put his hand in the fire); also took a big risk
opus-5.5* reasoning: iid with long ii plus -u. The idiom is usually about swearing to something with total confidence (ba7uTT iidi bin-naar), not simply getting into trouble.
gpt-6.1-sol* meaning_fix: put his hand in the fire; took a risk / vouched for someone
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: The expression can convey risking oneself or vouching for someone with absolute confidence. It does not specifically say that trouble actually resulted.
gemini-3.8-flash* reasoning: ط is emphatic T and doubles whole (TT); sun letter ن assimilates the article.
opus-5 reasoning: 7aTT with emphatic T and shadda; يد is iid in Palestinian with the -u possessive. The article assimilates to the sun letter ن.
opus-4.8 reasoning: Lit. put his hand in the fire = got himself in trouble; article to sun-letter n.
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: Literally 'he put his hand in the fire', meaning he took a risk or got into a dangerous situation. bi + il-naar is said bin-naar. ط is emphatic, so TT.
gpt-5.6-sol meaning_fix: vouched for it / staked his certainty on it
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: Putting one's hand in the fire idiomatically expresses absolute confidence or vouching, not getting into trouble.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Idiom for getting into trouble.

english: beat around the bush (lit: pound water into water)
meaning_fixes: futile effort / going round in circles achieving nothing (lit. pounding water, it stays water) / do something futile / waste effort or words (literally: pound water; it is still water) / futile effort / waste of time (lit: pounding water is water)
opus-5.5* meaning_fix: futile effort / going round in circles achieving nothing (lit. pounding water, it stays water)
opus-5.5* reasoning: The idiom (fuller form: da'' il-mayy w hiyye mayy) describes pointless work that changes nothing, not evasive speech. Shadda on ق gives '' in da''.
gpt-6.1-sol* meaning_fix: do something futile / waste effort or words (literally: pound water; it is still water)
gpt-6.1-sol* reasoning: The proverb is commonly heard as an imperative, du''. Its point is futile effort or unproductive repetition, rather than necessarily avoiding the issue.
gemini-3.8-flash* meaning_fix: futile effort / waste of time (lit: pounding water is water)

opus-5 meaning_fix: wasted his effort / got nowhere (lit: pounded water and it stayed water)
opus-5 reasoning: The idiom is about futile effort rather than evading a question, which is what beating around the bush means. The usual Levantine shapes are دق مي بمي or اللي بدق المي مي بتضل, so this wording is clipped and I am unsure of the intended reading.
opus-4.8 reasoning: دق with ق as glottal stop and shadda (da''); mayy = water. Idiom for pointless effort / beating around the bush.
sonnet-5.5 meaning_fix: pound water into water: do something pointless / waste effort or words
sonnet-5.5 reasoning: The idiom means futile effort or repeating the obvious, not quite 'beat around the bush' (lef w dawar). دق has a glottal ق with the shadda doubled, and water is mayy.
gpt-5.6-sol reasoning: Colloquial proverb about futile or evasive action; the supplied idiomatic gloss is plausible.
gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: An idiomatic expression.

gpt-5.6-sol meaning_fix: fucked around / messed around / acted silly

meaning_fixes: tin / tinplate / thin sheet metal; metal cans collectively

gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Tin can.

gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: In parentheses or so to speak.

gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Idiom for becoming aware.

gpt-5.6-terra reasoning: Means he is guilty.
